tips.title: Fixing Silvered Decals After They Have Dried
tips.text: Silvered decals happen when air is trapped under the decal. To fix after drying: apply Mr. Mark Softer generously over the decal, wait 10 minutes, then press gently with a damp cotton swab from the center outward to force air bubbles out. Repeat twice more with fresh solution. If silvering persists, carefully slit the decal film with a fresh hobby knife blade in a crosshatch pattern, apply setting solution again, and press flat. Once fully settled, seal with a gloss coat. For stubborn cases, replace the decal and reapply with stronger solutions like Daco Strong.

tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Plastic Kits
tips.text: To remove old paint from plastic kits without damaging the surface, use Citadel's Dettol Liquid Soap (not the gel). Dilute 1 part soap with 3 parts warm water, apply with a soft brush, let it soak for 10 minutes, then gently scrub with a soft toothbrush. Rinse with warm water and dry. For tougher cases, use Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to soften the paint, then gently scrape off with a scalpel.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To fix broken photo-etch parts, use CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue like Mr. Hobby's Super Clear. Apply a tiny drop on the inside of the joint, let it soak for 30 seconds, then press the parts together firmly. Wipe off excess glue immediately with a damp cotton swab. Once dry, reinforce the join with a small amount of Vallejo Plastic Putty, let it dry, then sand and paint as normal.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To recover a clogged airbrush, first disassemble it and soak the nozzle and needle in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 10 minutes. While soaking, use a soft brush to scrub the airbrush cup with a mild detergent. Reassemble the airbrush, then using Iwata's airbrush cleaning kit, pump 50% Vallejo Airbrush Thinner, 25% water, and 25% detergent through the airbrush until it's flowing smoothly. Finally, test spray with water to ensure no further clogs.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Plastic Parts
tips.text: To repair warped plastic parts, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes to soften. Gently bend the parts back into shape while submerged. Once shaped, lay them flat on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, then place in a oven at 140°F (60°C) for 10-15 minutes to set the new shape. Allow to cool before handling. For severe warping, consider using a hot air gun to gradually heat and bend the part into shape.
